verdict: Netflix's revenue rose 18% to $12.1B as paid memberships passed 325 million, and operating income jumped 30% to $3.0B — net income reached $2.4B even after about $60M of Warner Bros. bridge-loan costs tucked into interest expense.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; +17% at constant currency

segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — subscription streaming, plus the fast-growing ads business.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region, growing in line with North America this quarter (15% at constant currency).

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Cheaper plans are pulling in new households — up 15% as reported, 20% at constant currency.

segments.name: Asia-Pacific
segments.note: Mobile-first plans in price-sensitive markets — up 17% as reported, 19% at constant currency.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: The streaming platform, apps, recommendation systems and the new in-house ad-tech stack.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Netflix itself and winning subscribers — seasonally the biggest marketing quarter of the year.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company: legal, finance and offices.

takeaways.title: A membership milestone
takeaways.text: Netflix crossed 325 million paid memberships during the quarter — the last milestone it reported before moving to engagement and revenue as its headline measures.

takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than sales
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 30% YoY to $3.0B and the operating margin widened about two points to 24.5% — revenue growth of 18% dropped through to profit at a richer rate.

takeaways.title: Every region grew double digits
takeaways.text: UCAN and EMEA both grew 18%, Asia-Pacific 17% and Latin America 15% — broad growth, not one market carrying the quarter.

oneTimers: About $60M of costs related to the Warner Bros. bridge loan and associated financings were booked inside interest expense — one-off deal financing costs, not part of the streaming business, and not in Netflix's own guidance for the quarter.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $234M on Netflix's debt (including about $60M of Warner Bros. bridge-loan costs), partly offset by $45M of interest and other income — a net -$189M below operating profit.
